audit.whatIsWrong: Four chart rows disagree with the page's own why-text: rows 1 and 2 read Vladimir while whys[1] says 'Level 2 is even' and whys[2] says 'stays skill-based'; rows 3 and 5 read Skill while whys[3] says you have 'clear lane control again' and whys[5] says you out-scale him.
audit.why: The packet chart is Vladimir/Skill/Skill/Vladimir/Vladimir/Vladimir/Vladimir, matching the prose exactly.
audit.corrected: Rows 1, 2, 3 and 5 flipped as four matched full/content pairs in one atomic group.

audit.whatIsWrong: Unstoppable Force is named on twelve strings without its cooldown, and the level-6 spike says to pool it without saying whether pool will actually be up when it arrives.
audit.why: His R is 130s at rank 1 and 100s maxed, while Sanguine Pool is 28s falling to 16s — pool comes back four to eight times per ultimate. That ratio is why his level-6 spike does nothing to you, and it is far more convincing than the bare instruction to hold pool.
audit.corrected: Both cooldowns and the ratio written into spikes[1].text, dosFull[0].d and the cooldown block.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page calls his short-range defensive ability 'Thunderclap (E)' in two places. Thunderclap is his W; the E is Ground Slam. And Granite Shield — a shield worth 10% of his maximum health that recharges whenever he goes a few seconds without being hit — is never mentioned anywhere on the page.
audit.why: The name error is the exact class of mistake this audit exists to catch. Granite Shield is more important still: it is the reason poke that stops for a few seconds accomplishes nothing, and the reason you chip it off immediately before committing rather than letting it recharge between trades.
audit.corrected: Ground Slam replaces Thunderclap in spikes[0].text and early; Granite Shield's 10% absorb and its recharge condition written into spikes[0].text and wants.you[0]; Ground Slam's 7s and Seismic Shard's 8s flat added to the cooldown block.

audit.why: Transfusion is 600 range and Tides of Blood 600 — he is a short-range melee-adjacent drain, not a ranged caster. The relevant comparison is 600 against Ground Slam's 400, which is a real edge and states itself better with the numbers.

edits.before: - Malphite Unstoppable Force: matchup-defining — Un-dodgeable burst. Pool it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Unstoppable Force: 130s at rank 1, 100s maxed — Pool answers it. - Seismic Shard: 8s flat, and it steals your move speed. - Ground Slam: 7s. - Pool: 28s down to 16s, and it is spent only on his R.

edits.before: Un-dodgeable burst. Pool it. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: 130s at rank 1, and Pool's 2 untargetable seconds blank it entirely.

edits.before: You control the early lane. Malphite's only pre-6 poke is a mana-hungry Seismic Shard (Q) that shoves the wave, and his Thunderclap (E) is short-range and defensive. Stack E on him freely, sustain the Q chip with Transfusion, and abuse the fact that every Q he throws burns half his mana bar and pushes him into your poke.
edits.after: You control the early lane. Seismic Shard (Q) is his only pre-6 poke, an 8s 625-range shard that shoves the wave, and Ground Slam (E) is a 400-range defensive slam. Granite Shield absorbs 10% of his max health but recharges once he goes a few seconds unhit — chip it off, then commit, and never let him reset it.

edits.before: His R (Unstoppable Force) is a flank/all-in tool, not lane pressure, and you have the perfect answer: Sanguine Pool the exact instant he ults, and the knock-up whiffs while you take zero damage. Hold pool for his R every time and his level-6 spike does nothing to you.
edits.after: Unstoppable Force is 130s at rank 1 and it is a flank tool, not lane pressure — Sanguine Pool's 2 untargetable seconds answer it outright. Pool is 28s at rank 1 and 16s maxed, so it is up far more often than his ult: hold it for the R every time.

edits.before: You win the early lane outright. Malphite's only tool against you is Seismic Shard, which drains his mana and shoves the wave into your poke range, while Thunderclap is too short to threaten a ranged caster. Stack E on him, out-sustain the Q chip with Transfusion, and force him to choose between farming and going oom.
edits.after: You win the early lane outright. Seismic Shard costs up to 90 mana and shoves the wave into your poke range, while Ground Slam is a 400-range slam that cannot threaten you at 600. Stack Tides of Blood on him, out-sustain the Q chip with Transfusion, and force him to choose between farming and going oom.

edits.before: Stack E and poke while he wastes mana on Seismic Shard to clear
edits.after: Chip Granite Shield off before you commit — it is 10% of his health

notes: Two Thunderclap/Ground Slam slot errors fixed. The itemisation call on this page was already correct — both layers say his damage is magic and armour defends nothing — so I left it alone, as the mirror did. I did not write anything from the 'resistances-invalidated' missing rule: it is generated off Granite Shield's percentHealth flag, but a 10%-max-health shield is not resistance bypass, so the headline's framing would have been wrong. Thunderclap's on-hit and auto-reset flags are real but only matter if he walks into 400 range, which the rest of the page already tells you not to allow.
